sections.html:
Size: 120 cm SL.

Identification: Dorsum dull grey with pale green iridescence; maxillary band of teeth forms a continuous row with no break in midline. Snout protruding with upper jaw tooth bands partly exposed when mouth is closed; large median vomerine tooth plate.

Type locality: Thabo, Mekong River basin, Nongkhai Province, Thailand.
Asia: Mekong, Bangpakong and Chao Phraya basins. IUCN Red List: Least Concern (last assessed 2011).
The ultimate size of this fish, particularly when combined with its active swimming behaviour, makes it unsuitable for home aquaria.
Needs a large amount of open space for swimming room and some plants to help reduce the nervous nature of the fish.

Juveniles feed on prawns and insects; sub-adults and adults on prawns, insects and particularly mollusks, which are more predominant in stomach contents than in any other Pangasius species, and on plants.

Unreported. Migrates into the middle Mekong along the Thai-Lao border as water levels and turbidity begin to increase. Reproduces early in the flood season and juveniles of 6 to 7 cm are taken by late June.

There is no breeding report.

Etymology: the name Pangasius comes from a local (Bengali) name of the fish (pungas). The name conchophilus, a combination of the Latin concho (shell) and philus (loving), refers to the pronounced molluscivory of this species. Described by Roberts & Vidthayanon, 1991.
